items.name: Espacio Gropius
items.summary: A coworking space in Mendoza. The site is built around one action: booking a room. Every section routes there instead of describing the place and stopping.

items.name: Matix Digital
items.summary: Web development agency in Mendoza. Around 10 client sites since 2025. I take each one from the first conversation with the client through to delivery.

items.name: Casa Ladera
items.summary: A guesthouse in the Uco Valley. One enquiry form, and every section feeds it. There is no decent free photography of guest rooms, so each room is named after what its window faces.

items.name: Ávila Nieto Abogados
items.summary: A law firm site that answers one question: is this worth a call. It puts the fees, the response time and the confidentiality rule above the form instead of below it.

items.name: d2 Attention Test Calculator
items.summary: Scores the d2 attention test against age-banded reference values. Built for a psychology thesis where the correction was still done by hand. I found and fixed two calculation bugs in it: arguments passed in the wrong order, and numbers compared as strings.

items.name: Sales Management System
items.summary: Desktop sales system in Java over MySQL. I rewrote the write path to use PreparedStatement, which closed an SQL injection hole, and moved the database credentials out of the source code.

story.heading: The site got faster, then it started failing
body: A client site at Matix came to me for a performance pass. I optimized it and it did get faster. Then buffer errors started showing up that had not been there before.
I traced them to the WordPress configuration and fixed them there. The client kept the speed and lost the errors.
story.note: A blank page is the rare case. Most of the work is taking over a site that already exists and finding what is actually wrong with it.

steps.title: Start from the action
steps.body: What has to happen on this site: a booking, a call, a filled form. The layout comes out of that answer.

steps.title: Build it to be edited
steps.body: WordPress when the client needs to change things themselves. Hand-written HTML and CSS when speed is the point.

steps.title: Check it on a real phone
steps.body: Most visitors arrive on mobile. A site that only works on a laptop is not finished.

steps.title: Hand over the keys
steps.body: Domain, hosting and admin access go in the client's name, so you can walk away with the site whenever you want.

about.heading: About
body: I started in technical support and sales, moved into web development at Spika Solutions in 2023, and since 2025 I have been building client sites at Matix Digital.
Working with clients directly taught me the part a lot of developers never touch: agreeing on what the site actually has to do, and being the one who answers when something breaks at 8pm.
I am looking for a stable role on a team, remote, working on one product instead of ten clients. My English is C1, certified, and I take client calls without an interpreter.
